subject: Dedicated concurrency window request and queueing behavior negotiation (EdgeGrid)
messages:
From: Sara Noble <sara.noble@edgegrid.ai>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: partner@edgegrid.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: dedicated concurrency window + queueing guarantees

Hi Rohan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — EdgeGrid is excited about Redwood's latency profile. We're preparing our procurement request and have a few specific asks we need to validate before we can move to a signed reserved capacity commitment:

- A dedicated concurrency window (time-sliced reservation) for our peak batch scoring (20:00-22:00 PT daily) where we require sustained 1.2k reqs/s with median p99 latency <= 85ms for 512-token requests.
- Guaranteed reserved GPUs accessible only to EdgeGrid during that window (no preemption).
- Clarification on queueing behavior outside the window: what backpressure/fallbacks do you apply when demand spikes overlap the reserved window?

I've attached a short SLO request doc and a sample throughput spreadsheet. Can you confirm whether this is something Redwood can support with Dedicated and what the commercial implications look like?

Appreciate a quick run-through so we can calendar procurement approvals.

Best,
Sara
Sara Noble
Head of AI Platform
EdgeGrid
attachments: EdgeGrid_SLO_Request_v1.pdf, throughput-math.xlsx
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
To: Sara Noble <sara.noble@edgegrid.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated concurrency window + queueing guarantees

Hi Sara — thanks for outlining this clearly and sharing the spreadsheet.

Short answer: we can support a time-sliced dedicated concurrency window, but there are a few implementation choices that affect cost and guarantees. I'll summarize the options and then propose a next step: a 30-minute architecture call with infra and product.

Options to consider:
- Strict reservation (hard carve): allocate N reserved GPUs exclusively for EdgeGrid during 20:00-22:00 PT. Predictable but higher cost (unused capacity billed).
- Elastic reservation with guaranteed headroom: dedicate a smaller baseline pool plus an autoscale buffer that we prioritize for EdgeGrid requests during the window; lower committed cost, but residual preemption risk under extreme cluster pressure.
- Hybrid + local queueing: guarantee a reserved slot count and implement a fixed-length request queue for overflow that preserves p99 targets for admitted requests; long tails are rejected or overflow to a lower-cost model variant.

Questions for you before the call:
1) Is the 1.2k reqs/s steady across the full 2-hour window or highly spiky?
2) Are you willing to accept a small amount of queued requests (e.g., 200 concurrent) with clear retry behavior, or is zero-queueing mandatory?
3) Any regulatory constraint that prevents us from routing to a fallback model variant briefly?

I'll loop in Laura for pricing and Karthik on queueing policy details. Can you do Wed 16 Jun 2027 at 11:00 PT for a 30-min call?

—Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Sara Noble <sara.noble@edgegrid.ai>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: partner@edgegrid.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated concurrency window + queueing guarantees

Rohan — thanks for the quick reply. Answers below:

1) Traffic is bursty inside the window: typical baseline ~800 reqs/s with short bursts to 1.6k for up to 90s.
2) We cannot tolerate hard rejections during the window for production customers. A short fixed queue (200) with prioritized scheduling is acceptable if it does not push p99 over 100ms.
3) We cannot route PII-bearing workloads to a different model variant. All production inference must run on the same model family.

Wed 16 Jun 11:00 PT works for us. We'll have infra and procurement on the call.

Regards,
Sara
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
To: Sara Noble <sara.noble@edgegrid.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated concurrency window + queueing guarantees

Thanks for the answers — recap from today's call + proposed SLA language attached. Key engineering decisions we covered: 

- Reservation model: hybrid reserved GPUs (hard carve) sized for steady baseline (~900 reqs/s) plus prioritized autoscale buffer for bursts. Autoscale buffer will be billed as burst capacity with a separate rate; during extreme cluster pressure we will route to a cold-standby within the same model family located in the same region (no PII egress) only with your written consent.
- Queueing behavior: we will implement a prioritized in-memory queue for the window with configurable depth. EdgeGrid requested 200 concurrency queue; we propose admission control that caps queue wait at 1.5s (retries recommended after 2s). p99 measured for admitted requests will be guaranteed <= 95ms for 512-token requests.
- Preemption: reserved GPUs will not be preempted during the 20:00-22:00 PT window. If the autoscale buffer is exhausted, we will apply soft-fallbacks (cold-standby) instead of hard rejection.

Attachments: redwood_sla_draft_edgegrid.docx — draft commercial language and SLO table. Marissa, Laura — please confirm pricing uplift for the hard carve vs hybrid model and any billing minimums we should present. Karthik — can you confirm queue wait cap implementation feasibility?

Next steps:
1) Redwood to share SLA draft and pricing delta by EOD Thursday (17 Jun).
2) EdgeGrid procurement to provide preferred contract term (12/24/36 months) and any security addenda.
3) Follow-up call to review DocuSign-ready language on Friday if both sides agree.

—Rohan
attachments: redwood_sla_draft_edgegrid.docx
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated concurrency window + queueing guarantees

Thanks — reviewed the draft. Pricing summary for procurement: 

- Hard carve for the 2-hour daily window sized to 900 reqs/s baseline: $28k/mo (minimum 12-month commitment).
- Autoscale burst buffer pricing (pay-as-you-go) for short bursts above baseline: $0.025 per burst-unit (approx per 100 reqs/s-min).
- Hybrid recommended: baseline hard carve + burst buffer. Estimated blended uplift vs standard Dedicated: ~2.6x.

Marissa: add the minimum-billing and early-termination language. Karthik: note we need an infra ops runbook for "cold-standby" routing and a Showtime test before go-live.

I'll upload the pricing appendix to the shared Drive link and send a redlined SLA for EdgeGrid.

—Laura

1) Can Redwood put the queue wait cap (1.5s) and p99 <= 95ms for admitted requests into the SLO table with measurable metrics and weekly reporting?
2) We need a short acceptance test plan (Showtime) to validate p99 under synthetic spikes — can your infra team own that runbook and provide dates?

If you can include those in the redline by EOD Monday we can loop Legal and Procurement.
